title: Microsoft Teams: desk utilisation analytics in the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal
summary: Hold for corrections to the automation instructions. The licence assignment call omits the required empty removal collection, and the building-enablement call omits the value that enables buildings; its documentation link also does not document the accompanying check command. The rollout dates and published desk licensing figures are supported.

claims.quote: Teams admins can access utilization analytics for Teams bookable desks on Teams Pro Management portal, similar to analytics provided for meeting rooms on the portal today.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Desk licences are assigned through Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > desk account > Assign licenses.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, expand Users and select Active users.
- Search for the desk account you want to license and select it to open its details.
- Choose Assign licenses, select Microsoft Teams Shared Space, and save.

claims.claim: The printed Connect-Graph and Set-MgUserLicense call assigns a licence with only UserId and AddLicenses supplied to Set-MgUserLicense.
claims.quote: removeLicenses | Guid collection | A collection of skuIds that identify the licenses to remove. Required. Can be an empty collection.
claims.fix: Append -RemoveLicenses @() to Set-MgUserLicense in the front matter and rendered table. Keep the licence collection as a placeholder or use the cited assignment page's $addLicenses example, which supplies the empty removal collection. The scopes and cmdlet names are documented; the missing required collection is the defect.

claims.claim: Get-PlacesSettings -ReadFromPrimary and the printed bare Set-PlacesSettings -EnableBuildings provide the check/change operation, both documented by the linked Set-PlacesSettings page.
claims.quote:
You can enable building visibility in PowerShell:

Set-PlacesSettings -EnableBuildings 'Default:true'
claims.fix: Supply the required scope/value: Set-PlacesSettings -EnableBuildings 'Default:true' to enable buildings, or 'Default:false' to disable them. Keep Get-PlacesSettings -ReadFromPrimary as the check, but link it to https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/places/powershell/get-placessettings; the current Set-PlacesSettings docs URL contains no Get-PlacesSettings command. Update both front matter and rendered table.
